typed_core.why: identity — CORE; the seller entity/person being bound

typed_core.why: identity/disambiguator — CORE; LLC/corp/trust/estate determines which authority doc is required

typed_core.name: authorized_signer_title_or_capacity

typed_core.why: processor — whether the authority is still valid through closing

typed_core.name: loan_number

nested_lists.name: signatures_and_notary
nested_lists.shape_reason: execution blocks genuinely repeat (signer(s) + notary, typically <=2) and a processor confirms the authority itself is executed/notarized; a flat row (signer name + capacity + signed indicator + notary indicator + date) is tiny against the 16,384-token ceiling

fields.name: capacity
fields.why: processor — the capacity in which they signed

fields.name: signed_indicator
fields.why: processor — whether the block is signed

fields.name: notary_indicator
fields.why: processor — whether the block is notarized

rejected.name: delegation_or_substitution_authority
rejected.reason: edge-case CONDITIONAL string; no consumer, stays in catch-all

rejected.name: issuer_name / issuer_address / phone / email
rejected.reason: the issuer is the seller/entity already captured

rejected.name: form_number / effective / expiration / statement period
rejected.reason: not a standardized form; the authority dates are captured explicitly

encoding_variations: Authority arrives in several document types (corporate resolution, LLC operating-agreement excerpt, trust certificate, letters testamentary, POA) — authority_document_type + seller_entity_type fix which one and what it must contain
POA principal/agent vs authorized signer: on a POA the poa_agent should equal authorized_signer_name; capturing both lets the tag layer catch a mismatch
Scope may be general or transaction-specific — specific_property_or_transaction_authority disambiguates whether it reaches this closing

open_questions.q: Flatten signatures_and_notary vs nested list — there are usually <=2 signers plus a notary.
options: nested flat-row list (drafted) — safe for any count
open_questions.recommendation: (a) nested — the notary block is the proof the authority is itself validly executed, and the list is cheap GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): FLATTEN signatures to signature_present + signature_date — no signature nested list.

open_questions.q: seller_entity_type without an enum — the catalog provides no enum_values.
open_questions.recommendation: free str now; normalize if a rule later branches on entity type

notes: No rules read this document today (rule_count 0); there is no rule floor. This document proves that a named person may bind the seller (entity, trust, estate, or via POA) for the transaction. Fields earn a place by identity, disambiguation, or processor use.
No restricted fields on this doc. Signer/principal/agent names are standard sensitivity → identity fields, not registry PII. No _PII_FIELDS additions.
Prompt hint (doc-level): Do NOT decide whether the authority is sufficient — extract signer, capacity, document type, scope, dates, and revocation status; a processor/rule judges sufficiency.
